newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees Spanish mobile phone fee settlement.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees Spanish mobile phone fee settlement.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had approved a Spanish proposal to compensate GSM mobile phone consortium Airtel Movil for paying 85 billion pesetas ($583 million) to obtain an operating licence.
The government agreed to award Airtel a number of concessions after the Commission complained on the grounds that the country's first GSM operator, Telefonica de Espana, was not asked to pay a fee.

The Commission said in a statement that it had accepted the plan, under which Airtel would pay lower fees to connect to Telefonica's network, receive a licence for 25 years instead of 15 and be allowed to operate in the DCS 1800 frequency band without paying additional fees.
The Commission had argued that Airtel, a consortium of banks and international telecom operators, had been unfairly treated and the government should compensate it or charge Telefonica a similar fee.
The Commission said the economic impact of the measures proposed by the Spanish government were "broadly equivalent" to the licence fee paid by Airtel.
Partners in Airtel include Banco Central Hispano, Banco Santander, British Telecommunications Plc and Airtouch Communications Corp.
